vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 2.3.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate customer service reply template generator. The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a Python script that generates text-based responses for various e-commerce scenarios (presale, complaints, refunds, etc.) based on user input. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, network activity, file system modification, or malicious prompt injection; the code strictly performs string formatting and printing as described in `SKILL.md` and `tips.md`.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local generation of customer-service reply templates) matches the files and commands provided, but a prompt-injection pattern (unicode control characters) was detected in SKILL.md and the provided cs.sh file appears truncated in the submission — review the full script for hidden behavior before installing.

No unrelated binaries, cloud credentials, or unrelated install steps are requested.

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a local, instruction-only customer-service reply generator and is coherent with its description. Before installing or running it in a production environment: 1) Inspect the full scripts/cs.sh file (the provided listing was truncated). Search for network or system calls (e.g., imports/uses of requests, urllib, socket, subprocess/os.system, curl/wget, nc). 2) Remove or investigate any non-printable/unicode-control characters in SKILL.md and other files (these can be used to manipulate LLMs). 3) Run the script in an isolated/sandbox environment (no network) to confirm it only prints templates and does not exfiltrate data. 4) If you plan to let an agent call this autonomously, consider restricting model invocation or reviewing the script periodically. If you want, provide the complete scripts/cs.sh content and I can re-scan the full file for network calls or hidden behavior.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: SKILL.md was flagged for unicode control characters which can be used in prompt-injection attacks to influence LLM parsing. Such characters are not expected for a template-generation README. This could be accidental encoding noise, but it warrants manual inspection and removal before use.
